message.reasoning_content:
We need answer with JSON only. Need evaluate each story for Minimal criterion. Need be careful. Criterion: A user story contains nothing more than role, means, optional ends/rationale. Violation when core story includes comments, mock-up notes, implementation/testing hints, procedural notes, or other information external to story sentence.

We need inspect each BC-001 to BC-069. Need binary. We must return exactly 69 objects.

Need consider individual. Minimal violation if story includes more than role, means, ends/rationale. Many stories have typos, extra clauses, role/means/ends but no implementation notes. Need identify comments/mock-up notes/implementation/testing hints/procedural notes. Some include explicit UI details, field lists, URLs, workflow steps. Need judge.

Important: We should not penalize grammar issues unless adds info. Need evaluate minimal. Stories often written "As a X, I want to Y, so that Z." Even if wording flawed, no extra info? Some have additional clauses after "so that": "so that I can choose the right class, AND the trainer can tweet..." That's extra ends/rationale? optional ends? Role means and optional ends/rationale. Multiple ends okay? Minimal says contains nothing more than role, means, and optional ends/rationale. Multiple ends perhaps still ends/rationale, but if additional actor rationale maybe not? But Minimal does not prohibit compound rationale? It says optional ends/rationale. Could be multiple. But some have long detailed lists after "I want to have ..." that are part of means? Need decide.

Let's parse each.

BC-001: As a anonymoususer, I want to view a list of sponsors, so that I can thank all the awesome sponsors. Clean.

BC-002: Clean.

BC-003: As trainingcoordinator, I want to email all trainers at once from website for info and updates, so that It is easier to use. The "so that it is easier to use" vague but no extra. Means perhaps "for info and updates" part means. No violation.

BC-004: As attendee, I want to have a very clear map where buildings and rooms are, so that I can make it to class on time. Clean.

BC-005: As a trainer, I want to edit my training node myself, so that the training coordinators don't have to and links to slides. This has "and links to slides" after rationale? Actually sentence: "so that the training coordinators don't have to and links to slides." This is additional means/feature not role-means-ends? Contains "and links to slides" not as separate rationale but a desired thing. It is not implementation note but extra feature. Violation? Minimal: user story contains nothing more than role, means, and optional ends/rationale. Here "links to slides" appended to rationale, no so that. It includes additional requirement, not rationale. Could be violation. But is it external info? It says "and links to slides" suggests maybe user wants to edit training node and links to slides. This is an additional means. But user story can have one means? Minimal means role, means and optional ends. "and links to slides" is not end/rationale. Violation likely. Need decide.

BC-006: As a trainee, I want to limit to one registration per day per authenticated user, so that we don't have duplicate spaces. "per authenticated user" maybe system detail. But part of means. No external. Maybe role mismatch (trainee? wants limit per authenticated user) but minimal no. No violation.

BC-007: As trainingcoordinator, I want to have an admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee so that, so that we can see if attendend, refunded, no show. Duplicate "so that" but extra is rationale (registration statuses). No implementation. No violation? It contains "so that, so that" typo but still means and rationale. Not minimal violation.

BC-008: As attendee, I want to be added to a training waitlist, so that so they can be considered for a class. Clean? "so that so they" typo. No extra. No violation.

BC-009: As trainee, I want to must accept cancellation terms with a checkbox, so that they can be accountable.. "must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox" includes UI component "checkbox". Is that implementation/testing hint? The criterion explicitly "mock-up notes, implementation/testing hints" - specifying "with a checkbox" is UI detail/implementation. Is that beyond role, means, ends? Yes, it's implementation detail. Violation. Need evidence "with a checkbox". But maybe means can include checkbox? Minimal strict maybe yes. Should be violation.

BC-010: As trainingcoordinator, I want to tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists, so that so we don't loose money or spots. Contains "whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists" but means. "so that so" typo. No implementation. But "tie in a deadline to workflow" maybe not concrete. No violation.

BC-011: As trainee, I want to add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site, so that they can schedule their event experience. "if there is a schedule feature on the site" is conditional procedural? It is not a comment/mock-up but adds condition. Minimal? A user story contains role, means, optional ends. This includes condition "if there is a schedule feature" which is extra. It might be a requirement detail, not implementation. But "procedural notes" perhaps. Need judge. It says user wants to add to "my schedule" if feature exists. The "if there is a schedule feature on the site" is a condition/implementation context, not part of role means ends? Could be violation. But many stories include context. Need not overuse. Let's hold.

BC-012: As trainee, I want to see which trainings I have signed up for, so that they can schedule their event experience. Clean; pronoun mismatch not minimal.

BC-013: As trainer, I want to have a view that is attached to their training node that shows all attendee information Trainers can see all class attendance at first because there are so little trainers and they are trusted with privacy, so that the training coordinator doesn't have to do all the work to get login info for environment setup.
This includes extra explanatory note: "Trainers can see all class attendance at first because there are so little trainers and they are trusted with privacy" within the story, and ends with "to get login info for environment setup."
